sources.notes: Inert schedule(parameters, closure) definitions, immediate invocation, dynamic convergence, and one-time instances use the shared graph.

Hosted applications lower workflow cron through the shared schedule graph and authorize the ApplicationHost caller. Workflow-only applications emit a focused schedule-control worker, exact workflow-gateway authorization, and target-specific fixed-schedule resources; qualified external schedules are excluded. Generated-worker live Hatchet evidence remains provider qualification rather than source-contract evidence.

Hosted and workflow-only durable future starts lower to a shared one-time occurrence through the managed application or focused schedule-control boundary. Exact live Hatchet occurrence and provider-resource cleanup remain provider qualification evidence.

Function-native dynamic schedules converge through the shared graph, persist canonical desired state before provider projection, and are served by either the managed application host or the generated workflow-only schedule-control worker. Generated-worker restart/live lifecycle remains provider qualification evidence.
Processor checkpoint, partition, and consumer lifecycle remain processor semantics and are not exposed as public schedule parity.
Alarm authority, actor identity, persisted timer state, and turn ordering remain actor-owned.
Image/command CronJobs are target-specific infrastructure and never claim function-native parity.

providers.remaining: Bounded history policy and fresh generated-product restart/teardown qualification. Canonical persistence and admitted-occurrence recovery are covered deterministically.

Bounded instance ceiling enforcement plus exact scheduled-time, duplicate occurrence, retry receipt, and generated schedule-control worker lifecycle evidence. OrbStack now proves PostgreSQL-authority restart recovery, create/no-op, drift repair, UID-preserving update, disable, idempotent delete, and owned cleanup.

Deterministic integration, clean packed consumption, and OrbStack PostgreSQL occurrence recovery are implemented. Real Hatchet installed through TypeKro/Alchemy still needs fixed/dynamic/one-time firing, update, disable, deletion, provider interruption, drift repair, and leak-free teardown evidence before live qualification.

Deterministic tests prove interrupted provider projection recovery, but real-AWS create/no-op/update/one-time/disable/duplicate/retry/DLQ/drift/interruption/delete and cost evidence remains; all-bounded remains an explicit compatibility rejection.
